title: Hotline 1.9 protocol documentation gap register
method: Documentation gap audit of corrected sources and prior static validity ledger; no new Ghidra queries, packet captures, mxd tests or client execution in this audit.

gaps.title: Define the supported 1.9 subset

sources.heading: Hotline Server Protocol 1.9: Transactions and Functionality Guide
Open compatibility gaps and QA requirements

gaps.question: Which of the 45 requests and server notifications must mxd implement now, defer explicitly, or reject, and which peer profiles are acceptance targets?
gaps.implementation_impact: An open-ended baseline cannot define feature completion or compatible rejection behaviour.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish an operation-by-profile scope matrix with required, deferred and excluded states, including replies to unsupported operations.

gaps.title: Canonical transaction and field schemas
gaps.question: For every in-scope request, reply and notification, which fields are required, optional, conditional or repeatable, with what widths and value domains?
gaps.implementation_impact: Lists of fields that a handler reads are not sufficient to build a compatible encoder or validator.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide a schema registry for the core operations, marking each remaining unknown with a gap ID; include direction, cardinality, width, conditions and defaults.

gaps.title: Error-code and failure-outcome registry
gaps.question: Which statuses, field-100 forms and connection outcomes apply to each failure, including errors in operations without a normal ACK?
gaps.implementation_impact: Implementations cannot distinguish recoverable failure, success, silent rejection and impending disconnect consistently.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document a failure table and representative bytes for authentication, permission, missing-object, malformed-request and unsupported-operation cases.

gaps.title: Transaction ID lifecycle and correlation
gaps.question: Are zero, duplicate, wrapped or reused IDs accepted, how are client and server ID spaces separated, and how are unsolicited replies treated?
gaps.implementation_impact: Correlation and reassembly can attach a reply or payload to the wrong outstanding operation.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify ID allocation, lifetime, wrap/reuse and notification correlation rules; exercise zero, collision and late-reply cases.

gaps.title: Connection timers and liveness

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: What are the handshake, login, agreement, idle and partial-frame deadlines, and what traffic resets them?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client can wait forever or disconnect a compatible session prematurely without a liveness contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide a timer/state table with units, reset conditions, configurable values and close outcomes, distinguishing native observations from mxd limits.

gaps.title: Complete direction and reply-contract catalogue

sources.heading: Sending a Chat Message (Transaction 105) – Client Initiates
Leaving a Chat Room (Transaction 116) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: Which operation/direction/session-state combinations are accepted, and what direct success/error replies or subsequent notifications belong to each? The current ACK/Push prose is not a complete catalogue.
gaps.implementation_impact: Implementers must infer dispatch direction and negative-outcome rules from scattered handler descriptions rather than one complete contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish an operation-by-direction/state table distinguishing direct success replies, error replies, emitted notifications and acceptance/completion semantics.

gaps.title: Allowed operations by session state

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: What can be sent before authentication, after login ACK, while agreement is pending, after early completion and during shutdown?
gaps.implementation_impact: The guide has transaction descriptions but no complete dispatch/state contract for a server implementation.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish a state/operation table including invalid transitions, replayed login/agreement requests and state-specific failures, backed by traces or dispatcher analysis.

gaps.title: Handshake failures and stream boundaries
gaps.question: How are short, long, pipelined, wrong-magic, wrong-version or unsupported-sub-version handshakes consumed, replied to and closed?
gaps.implementation_impact: The happy-path twelve/eight-byte layouts do not specify initial stream recovery or rejection.
gaps.closure_criteria: Record positive and negative handshake exchanges with exact byte consumption, response status, pipelining behaviour and closure order.

gaps.title: Sub-version 3 and direct HTXF relationship
gaps.question: When does the TRTP sub-version-3 path apply, on which endpoint, and how does it relate to a direct sixteen-byte HTXF header?
gaps.implementation_impact: An implementer could perform the wrong handshake on a transfer socket despite knowing each observed magic.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace the two entry paths and document complete endpoint-specific sequences, transitions and fixture bytes.

gaps.title: Listening endpoints and data-port arithmetic
gaps.question: How are control/data listeners selected and configured, and is the data port always the base port plus one in this build?
gaps.implementation_impact: File-transfer connection setup cannot be derived from a tentative port convention.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace listener creation and configuration; document endpoint mapping, exceptions and verified client connection examples.

gaps.title: Frame, transaction and buffering limits
gaps.question: Is the image's 2 MiB value changed at runtime, does it bound a frame or aggregate transaction, and how are totals, fragments and concurrent buffers limited?
gaps.implementation_impact: The existing image constant does not define safe or interoperable allocation and framing boundaries.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document native comparisons/configuration and explicit mxd limits with inclusive boundaries, overflow checks and boundary fixtures.

gaps.title: Fragment reassembly edge cases
gaps.question: What happens when type/total changes, fragments interleave, lengths overrun or underfill, transactions are abandoned, or a partial frame ends in EOF?
gaps.implementation_impact: A codec implementing only ordinary concatenation has no specified outcome for common malformed or interrupted input.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish reassembly invariants and a test matrix covering keys, length consistency, overshoot, underflow, abandonment and partial TCP delivery.

gaps.title: Accepted envelope values and reserved bytes
gaps.question: How are nonzero flags, reply markers other than zero/one, nonzero request error words, unsupported types and nonzero reply types handled?
gaps.implementation_impact: Writer conventions do not define the input-validation contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify accepted and rejected header values for each direction and their failure outcomes, supported by receiver checks and negative fixtures.

gaps.title: TLV structural validation
gaps.question: What happens with a missing count, count/length mismatch, truncated values, trailing bytes, zero field IDs, unknown fields or maximum field counts?
gaps.implementation_impact: The record shape alone is insufficient for a deterministic parameter decoder.
gaps.closure_criteria: Define exact consumption, bounds, unknown-field and trailing-data rules; add byte fixtures at every boundary and mismatch class.

gaps.title: Field-specific scalar types
gaps.question: Which numeric fields permit one/two/four bytes, which are fixed-width or signed, and how are booleans, sentinel values and invalid widths interpreted?
gaps.implementation_impact: The generic reader's three-byte-to-zero behaviour could be mistaken for a valid zero or applied to a fixed-width field.
gaps.closure_criteria: Give each core scalar an explicit wire type, allowed widths/range and invalid-width outcome, including references and privilege bitmaps.

gaps.title: Absent, empty and zero-valued fields
gaps.question: Which operations distinguish an omitted field, a zero-length TLV, an empty string and numeric zero, and what defaults are applied?
gaps.implementation_impact: The native writer omits empty fields while documented readers sometimes reset state when fields are absent.
gaps.closure_criteria: Add per-field presence/default tables and fixtures for all four cases, especially credentials, settings and partial account updates.

gaps.title: Repeated scalar fields and ordering
gaps.question: Beyond observed list/invitation cases, are duplicate scalars rejected, first-wins, last-wins or accumulated, and is order meaningful?
gaps.implementation_impact: Preserving repetitions is necessary but does not determine how each schema resolves ambiguous duplicates.
gaps.closure_criteria: Define multiplicity and ordering by transaction/field and test repeated scalars, interleaved repeated records and reordered inputs.

gaps.title: Text encoding and transformations

sources.heading: Receiving a Chat Message (Transaction 106) – Server Initiates
Listing Files in a Folder (Transaction 200) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: Which charset, normalization, NUL handling and line-ending rules apply to credentials, names, paths, chat, news and error text?
gaps.implementation_impact: A generic UTF-8 or XOR heuristic can change valid native text and fail to round-trip names or message content.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish per-field byte/string rules with non-ASCII, embedded-NUL, CR/LF and complemented-credential fixtures from identified peers.

gaps.title: Semantic length limits and truncation

sources.heading: Sending a Chat Message (Transaction 105) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: What byte/character limits and truncation or rejection rules apply to every name, password, message, subject, comment and body?
gaps.implementation_impact: The 65,535-byte TLV limit does not describe smaller buffers, truncation, multibyte strings or advertised transfer sizes.
gaps.closure_criteria: Record field-specific limits and units, max/max-plus-one behaviour and aggregate limits, preserving native versus mxd-policy distinctions.

gaps.title: Date and timestamp semantics

sources.heading: Reading a News Article (Transaction 400) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: What epoch/units apply to the supplied filesystem value, how do nonzero milliseconds and other years work, and is news date 330 equivalent?
gaps.implementation_impact: The observed 1904/zero/value structure cannot yet be converted or compared reliably across all date fields.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace each date producer/consumer and document epoch, timezone, units, range and conversion fixtures including rollover cases.

gaps.title: ACK versus completion, durability and retry

sources.heading: Sending an Instant Message (Transaction 108) – Client Initiates
Posting a News Article (Transaction 410) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: When an ACK precedes routing or mutation side effects, what has it committed to, and what can fail or be retried afterwards?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client may treat acceptance as delivered/durable success and duplicate non-idempotent operations on reconnect.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify completion points, post-ACK failure signalling, persistence and retry/idempotency rules per operation with disconnect-boundary fixtures.

gaps.title: Native nonempty-password encoding
gaps.question: What exact bytes does the 1.9 server expect for nonempty passwords in login and account mutation, independent of SynHX's helper?
gaps.implementation_impact: The guide cannot yet supply a working nonempty-password authentication fixture.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace account storage and comparisons, then capture successful and failed logins plus account changes using known nonempty credentials.

gaps.title: Login-name lookup and guest fallback
gaps.question: Are absent, empty, NUL-containing or differently cased logins equivalent; how are complemented bytes normalized and guest permissions chosen?
gaps.implementation_impact: The guest-name path and account-name transformations are not a complete authentication lookup contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document transformation order, canonicalization and absent/empty/unknown account outcomes using lookup-helper evidence and fixtures.

gaps.title: Client-version and optional login inputs
gaps.question: Are fields 160/102/104 mandatory, what defaults apply if omitted or malformed, and does saved version affect anything besides the named banner/news paths?
gaps.implementation_impact: A field-read list can be mistaken for required input and can select the wrong login-completion path.
gaps.closure_criteria: Supply a login input-condition table covering presence, widths, zero, version boundaries and each dependent feature without using version as conclusive client identity.

gaps.title: Complete login/agreement state machine
gaps.question: What are the exact ACK, 109, 354, 122 and 301 ordering and state transitions for early completion, ordinary acceptance, no agreement, repeated 121 and delayed acceptance?
gaps.implementation_impact: Two observed completion paths do not yet define a deterministic interoperable session sequence.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide state/sequence tables and captured fixtures for each configured path, including duplicate/out-of-state requests and visibility timing.

gaps.title: Meaning and lifetime of login extras
gaps.question: What are field 161's identifier semantics, widths and invalidation rules, and field 162's encoding/limits; how do they relate to banner 122 and download 212?
gaps.implementation_impact: An implementation can send the right IDs with incompatible values or stale banner identity.
gaps.closure_criteria: Define the value schemas, configuration sources and change/lifetime rules with sample configured/no-banner replies.

gaps.title: Agreement absence, bypass and text rules
gaps.question: When is 154 emitted, how do absent/empty/unreadable agreement text and account bypass privileges behave, and must a client send 121 after early completion?
gaps.implementation_impact: Agreement omission or bypass may produce a different readiness flow than the prose implies.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document the configuration/account condition matrix and its wire/state outcomes; include absent, empty and configured agreement fixtures.

gaps.title: Banner metadata variants and lifecycle
gaps.question: Which four-byte type tags and field-153 representations are valid, when are they required, and how does an early-completed session obtain metadata without a later 121?
gaps.implementation_impact: The URL and image paths are described conditionally without a full schema or availability sequence.
gaps.closure_criteria: Enumerate supported type/field combinations, conditions and ordering, including no-banner, URL, image and metadata changes.

gaps.title: Settings update defaults and persistence
gaps.question: Which omitted/empty 102/104/113/215 values reset, preserve or derive state, and what changes are session-only or durable?
gaps.implementation_impact: The warning against patch semantics still leaves callers unable to construct a safe partial update.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document field-by-field update/default/persistence rules and before/after state plus emitted-301 fixtures.

gaps.title: Settings option edge cases and automatic-response defaults

sources.heading: Sending an Instant Message (Transaction 108) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: How are unknown 113 bits, auto-response enable/disable transitions, missing 215 and default-response text handled across 121 and 304?
gaps.implementation_impact: The three known bits do not define all transitions or distinguish stored text from active automatic response.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify bit acceptance and transition tables, default text/encoding, and enable/disable/update fixtures without conflating PM enumerants.

gaps.title: Complete privilege bitmap registry
gaps.question: What do all unlisted bits, including 18/19 and 41-63, mean, and which bits are reserved, ignored or preserved?
gaps.implementation_impact: The corrected observed subset cannot support full account editing or a complete permission model.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish a 64-bit MSB-first registry with per-bit evidence, unknown/reserved distinctions and serialization/enforcement fixtures.

gaps.title: Privilege composition and inheritance
gaps.question: How do general, folder and news helpers combine account rights, path-specific rules, inheritance and administrator overrides?
gaps.implementation_impact: Knowing a bit number does not establish which request on which object is authorized.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document decision tables for the three helper domains, including inherited/overridden rights and forbidden operations.

gaps.title: User, room, article and reference identifier lifetimes

sources.heading: Retrieving the User List (Transaction 300) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: What are each ID's wire width, allocation scope, sentinel values, wrap/reuse rules and persistence across reconnects or restart?
gaps.implementation_impact: A shared numeric value can be misinterpreted across object/session lifetimes or truncated using the wrong width.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide a domain-specific identifier registry with allocation/reuse rules and stale-ID/wrap fixtures.

gaps.title: Colour/status bitmap semantics

sources.heading: Retrieving the User List (Transaction 300) – Client Initiates
User Appearance and Updates (Transaction 301 & 302) – Server Initiates

gaps.question: What does each field-112/packed-roster status bit represent and when does it change relative to settings, privileges or away state?
gaps.implementation_impact: Clients can decode record lengths yet display or propagate incompatible presence state.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace status construction and publish a separate status-bit registry plus state-transition examples.

gaps.title: Roster and update ordering

sources.heading: Retrieving the User List (Transaction 300) – Client Initiates
User Appearance and Updates (Transaction 301 & 302) – Server Initiates

gaps.question: Does 301 include the subject user, when is a session visible in 300, and how are snapshots ordered against concurrent changes and 354?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client can miss or double-apply a user when initial roster and updates overlap.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document eligibility, recipient and ordering rules, with initial login, rename and snapshot-race event traces.

gaps.title: Disconnect notification and cleanup

sources.heading: User Appearance and Updates (Transaction 301 & 302) – Server Initiates
Leaving a Chat Room (Transaction 116) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: Which teardown paths emit 302, which fields/recipients are used, and when are rooms, queued transfers and IDs cleaned up?
gaps.implementation_impact: The known explicit-leave path does not specify global disconnect consistency.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace normal EOF, timeout, kick and failure teardown, then document and fixture 302 and associated room/transfer cleanup ordering.

gaps.title: Diagnostic-text output contract
gaps.question: Are the 303 text labels, line endings, address representation and transfer summaries stable protocol content or build/configuration-dependent presentation?
gaps.implementation_impact: An implementation may promise exact native text or parse it as a stable structure without evidence.
gaps.closure_criteria: Define mandatory versus descriptive content, encoding/limits and representative replies; explicitly state whether exact textual parity is required.

gaps.title: Room access and main-chat membership

Joining a Chat Room (Transaction 115) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: Is the main room implicit, and what authorizes join, send, invite, topic edit or administrative access to a private room?
gaps.implementation_impact: The presence of a room ID and bit-11 check does not specify all membership/permission requirements.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish room-state and permission tables with member/non-member, owner/admin, missing-room and main-chat cases.

gaps.title: Invitation lifecycle and partial failures
gaps.question: How are duplicate target UIDs, declined/expired invitations, repeated joins, disconnected invitees and mixed valid/invalid target lists handled?
gaps.implementation_impact: Repeated UID support alone does not define whether a request partially succeeds or how invitation state expires.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document 112/113/114 lifecycle, recipient outcomes, atomicity and retries; include mixed-target and disconnect/reject fixtures.

gaps.title: Room snapshot and notification ordering

sources.heading: Joining a Chat Room (Transaction 115) – Client Initiates
Leaving a Chat Room (Transaction 116) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: When is subject 115 omitted versus empty, does the joining user appear in the returned roster, and how do 117/118 interleave with join/leave replies?

gaps.title: Subject update validation
gaps.question: Who may change a topic, what are the maximum length/encoding rules, and do absent and empty 115 both clear it?
gaps.implementation_impact: The current description establishes a setter/send site without a complete authorized update contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document topic permissions and input/default rules with denied, empty, omitted, boundary-length and successful notifications.

gaps.title: Chat formatting and option 109

sources.heading: Sending a Chat Message (Transaction 105) – Client Initiates
Receiving a Chat Message (Transaction 106) – Server Initiates

gaps.question: What are option-109 values/defaults, exact server formatting, newline/NUL handling and recipient rules for main versus room chat?
gaps.implementation_impact: The delivered text cannot be reproduced from raw client input using the current guide.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace formatting and fan-out helpers and record ordinary/action/system, multiline and permission-denied examples with byte-level text rules.

gaps.title: Private-message routing truth table

sources.heading: Sending an Instant Message (Transaction 108) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: How do options 1-4, both peers' refusal/automatic-response flags, empty text and quoted field 214 combine, including post-ACK rejection or automatic-response loops?
gaps.implementation_impact: The guide lists enumerants but does not fully specify who receives what in each state.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish a sender/recipient/options decision table with ACKs and emitted 104 fields for each supported case.

gaps.title: Type-104 variant schemas

sources.heading: Receiving a Private Message (Transaction 104) – Server Initiates
Sending a Chat Message (Transaction 105) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: Which fields identify user messages, server/admin notices, refusals and kick notices; are sender UID/name/options mandatory in each variant?

gaps.closure_criteria: Define discriminators and per-variant required/optional fields, with fixtures for each known producer.

gaps.title: Flood, spam and throttling outcomes

sources.heading: Sending a Chat Message (Transaction 105) – Client Initiates
Sending an Instant Message (Transaction 108) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: What counters, windows, limits and reset conditions cause rejection, delayed handling, ACK-then-close or disconnection for each operation?
gaps.implementation_impact: Ordinary traffic and retry policies can trigger undocumented native rate behaviour.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace per-operation limits/configuration and publish bounded timing/rate fixtures plus explicit mxd policy where parity is intentionally different.

gaps.title: Legacy-board data and update contract
gaps.question: What are the aggregate 101 format, append/replace rules for 103, post size limits, persistence and 102 update ordering/recipients?
gaps.implementation_impact: Keeping the old board in scope does not yet provide an interoperable read/post/update implementation.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document board serialization and mutation semantics with multi-post, empty, boundary-size and update-recipient fixtures.

gaps.title: Structured path format

sources.heading: Listing Files in a Folder (Transaction 200) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: What are the counts, component records, reserved bytes, root representation, limits and normalization rules for fields 202/212/325, and do those fields share a grammar?
gaps.implementation_impact: Control transactions cannot address filesystem or news objects from unspecified opaque bytes.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace path encoders/resolvers and provide separate field grammars and root/nested/non-ASCII/invalid-component fixtures; prove any claimed equivalence.

gaps.title: File-list record layout

sources.heading: Listing Files in a Folder (Transaction 200) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: What are the exact field-200 offsets, metadata/tag meanings, size widths, entry kinds, sort order and empty-list representation?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client cannot render or navigate file listings from the current field ID alone.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify the nested record grammar and listing order with file/folder/alias/non-ASCII/empty/multiple-entry fixtures.

gaps.title: File-info variant matrix
gaps.question: Which fields and widths occur for files, folders, aliases and special items, including descriptive 205/206, raw 213 and size/date omissions?
gaps.implementation_impact: Removing the universal four-character assumption still leaves multiple incompatible response schemas.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish a target-kind/field-presence/type matrix with representative metadata and empty/unknown-value cases.

gaps.title: Delete semantics and failures
gaps.question: Can 204 remove nonempty folders, which errors apply to missing/root/protected targets, and what state/notifications follow a partial filesystem failure?
gaps.implementation_impact: A successful ACK is not a complete destructive-operation contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace deletion helpers and define permission, recursion, failure/atomicity and refresh outcomes with controlled fixtures.

gaps.title: Folder creation semantics

sources.heading: Creating a New Folder (Transaction 205) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: How are name/path defaults, existing names, invalid names, missing parents and per-folder privilege checks handled by 205?
gaps.implementation_impact: An encoder can issue a valid TLV request but cannot predict creation or error outcomes.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document input conditions, conflicts, permission and success/error responses for 205 with exact fixtures.

gaps.title: Rename/comment partial updates
gaps.question: Do omitted/empty 210 and 211 preserve, clear or reject values, and what happens when one permitted sub-operation succeeds and another fails?
gaps.implementation_impact: The guide allows both fields without defining partial success, atomicity or comment/rename permission combinations.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish the field-presence/permission/conflict matrix and before/after outcomes for rename-only, comment-only and combined requests.

gaps.title: Move collision and metadata behaviour
gaps.question: How do destination conflicts, aliases, cross-volume moves and interrupted filesystem operations affect 208 and its ACK/error result?
gaps.implementation_impact: The operation name does not establish overwrite, rollback or metadata preservation rules.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document resolver and move outcomes, including same-location, collision and partial-failure fixtures; bound any platform-specific semantics.

gaps.title: Alias creation and resolution
gaps.question: What alias object is created, how is its name chosen, and when do listing/info/download resolve its target rather than expose the alias itself?
gaps.implementation_impact: Portable symlink assumptions can produce different list, metadata and transfer results.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace alias creation/resolution and document source/destination/default-name rules with live, missing-target and alias-to-alias cases.

gaps.title: Sixteen-byte HTXF header and reference matching
gaps.question: What are every offset/width, type value, reserved field and reference-matching rule, and how do unknown, expired or other-session references fail?
gaps.implementation_impact: No interoperable transfer handshake can be encoded from the current partial description.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish the complete header plus upload/download/banner matching and failure rules with valid/invalid reference and type fixtures.

gaps.title: Flattened file and fork stream
gaps.question: What are stream headers, metadata/fork records, lengths, padding, order and termination for ordinary Mac files versus raw/preview transfers?
gaps.implementation_impact: The control ACK does not specify actual file contents or preserve resource forks.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace transfer workers and publish byte grammars plus data/resource-fork, empty-file and metadata round-trip fixtures.

gaps.title: Download and preview response conditions
gaps.question: Which 204 values/defaults choose each mode, how are 108/207 calculated and when are 107/116 omitted or mandatory?
gaps.implementation_impact: A successful zero-size response or differing sizes cannot yet be interpreted consistently.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document mode and response-presence/size calculation tables with zero-size, preview, ordinary and queued fixtures.

gaps.title: Resume-data format and offset negotiation
gaps.question: What is the nested field-203 grammar, which forks/offsets it covers, and how are mismatch, completed and missing partial files handled?
gaps.implementation_impact: Neither upload nor download resume can be implemented from a field label and mode value.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace both directions and publish offset/fork validation and continuation fixtures, including fresh/resumed/completed and inconsistent state.

gaps.question: What are entry/path records, actions, traversal order, aggregate counts/sizes, skips and resume transitions for 210?
gaps.implementation_impact: The known initiation fields do not describe a recursive transfer implementation.

gaps.title: Folder-upload stream state machine

gaps.title: Queue notification 211 and scheduling

gaps.title: Transfer completion, failure and persistence

gaps.implementation_impact: A transfer can appear complete while lacking data or leave incompatible resumable state after failure.

gaps.implementation_impact: A known top-level field switch does not permit decoding or justify a displayed-version mapping.

gaps.implementation_impact: The correction to one containing field still leaves the article list impossible to decode.

gaps.question: What precisely do 331/332/335/336 identify, what are sentinel/end conditions, which flavours work and how is 330 constructed?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client cannot traverse threads or interpret all article data from field names alone.

gaps.title: Posting and new-article discovery

sources.heading: Posting a News Article (Transaction 410) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: How do omitted/zero 326, flags 334, supported flavours and body limits affect creation, and how is the resulting ID or update discovered after ACK?
gaps.implementation_impact: Posting can succeed without any specified way to locate the new article or distinguish parent relationships.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish post field/default and flag tables plus discovery/notification/persistence behaviour for new threads, replies and invalid requests.

gaps.title: Recursive article deletion

sources.heading: Deleting a News Article (Transaction 411) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: What values/widths does 337 accept, and how are descendants, orphans, navigation IDs and notifications updated on success or partial failure?
gaps.implementation_impact: The guide intentionally removed guessed deletion semantics but provides no replacement contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace deletion/index helpers and document nonrecursive/recursive outcomes with parent, leaf and failure fixtures.

gaps.title: News hierarchy and structure mutations
gaps.question: What nesting/type/depth rules apply, how are paths and name fields interpreted, and what happens on create/delete conflicts or subtree failures?
gaps.implementation_impact: A fixed four-tier assumption was withdrawn without a validated structural model for mxd.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish object/path grammars and 380/381/382 permission/conflict/recursive-effect tables with nested and failure fixtures.

gaps.title: Account field 111
gaps.question: What is field 111's wire type, presence/default rule, stored meaning and effect on 350/353?
gaps.implementation_impact: The documented account schema explicitly contains a field mxd cannot yet interpret or preserve correctly.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace reads/storage/use of 111 and add an account field schema with absent, empty and representative-value fixtures.

gaps.title: Account update, placeholder and identity rules
gaps.question: How are target login, rename, absent/empty password, literal x, duplicate names, protected-account deletion and partial updates handled?
gaps.implementation_impact: Treating the 352 placeholder as an unchanged-password token could overwrite credentials or target the wrong account.
gaps.closure_criteria: Define 350-353 mutation/default/atomicity rules with existing-password preservation, literal-x, rename/conflict and protected-delete fixtures.

gaps.title: Account changes and active sessions
gaps.question: When do edited privileges, names or passwords affect current sessions, does deletion disconnect them, and what 354/301 notifications occur?
gaps.implementation_impact: Stored account state and live authorization may diverge in ways clients and tests cannot predict.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace account/session propagation and record live-edit/delete event sequences and persistence across reconnect/restart.

gaps.title: Kick/ban option branches
gaps.question: What exactly do options 1 and 2 do, including identity matching, ranges/duration, optional data 101, reconnection and protected users?
gaps.implementation_impact: Enumerated branches were observed but account-ban/IP-ban semantics remain guesses.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace both ban helpers and publish option/outcome/expiry/protection rules with kick-only and both branch fixtures.

gaps.title: Standalone transaction 111

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: Does any native producer actually emit 111, under which conditions, with what fields and delivery/closure ordering?
gaps.implementation_impact: A retained catalogue entry cannot yet be implemented or declared absent with confidence.
gaps.closure_criteria: Locate a producer and capture its schema/sequence, or document a bounded negative-search result and an explicit support decision.

gaps.title: Server-originated broadcast and eligibility
gaps.question: Does a console-generated broadcast use the same 355 schema, and which connected/logged-in/refusing users receive each origin's broadcast?
gaps.implementation_impact: The validated client-request path does not establish all advertised admin/server initiation cases.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace console and fan-out paths and publish origin/recipient/field tables with self-recipient and session-state fixtures.

gaps.title: Request 348 schema and purpose

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: What does 348 do, what fields and privileges apply, and how are its potentially nested account records serialized?
gaps.implementation_impact: An observed dispatcher entry cannot be advertised as a supported account operation from its number alone.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace handler/helper paths and provide operation semantics, request/reply grammar and representative success/error fixtures.

gaps.title: Request 349 schema and batch outcomes

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: What indexed/transitive fields does 349 consume, how are batch entries delimited, and are failures atomic or per-entry?
gaps.implementation_impact: Implementing guessed batch semantics can mutate only part of a request with no specified result.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace the handler and publish batch framing, permission/default/partial-error rules and mixed-success fixtures.

gaps.title: Request 500 purpose and scheduling

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: Is 500 a liveness operation or something else, who sends it and when, and does its ACK affect idle deadlines?
gaps.implementation_impact: Naming it a keepalive or scheduling it periodically would invent a contract from an empty-ACK handler.
gaps.closure_criteria: Identify client/server call sites or captures, document its purpose/timing/state eligibility, and explicitly scope support.

gaps.title: Identified peer corpus and fallback classifier

sources.heading: Open compatibility gaps and QA requirements

gaps.question: Which client builds are acceptance targets, what stable evidence distinguishes them after removing sub-version 2, and what is the unknown-peer fallback?
gaps.implementation_impact: Correcting a bad discriminator does not supply a replacement compatibility policy.
gaps.closure_criteria: Create a hashed client/capture corpus and evidence-based profile/fallback rules; retain reported version values separately from proven identities.

gaps.title: Client tolerance of extra fields
gaps.question: Which identified clients accept 161/162, 122, native roster output and the SynHX subject addition, and when is an omission policy necessary?
gaps.implementation_impact: The matrix cannot justify compatibility-specific reply changes from another server's output alone.
gaps.closure_criteria: Run a peer-by-field acceptance matrix and record actual failures/tolerance before selecting omission/default policies.

gaps.title: Heuristic text-decoding policy
gaps.question: Will mxd retain text XOR heuristics, on which fields/states, and how does it handle valid non-UTF-8 or ambiguous plaintext without irreversible mode changes?
gaps.implementation_impact: Credential complementing does not decide a general message/news decoder and heuristics may not identify peers.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document the policy decision and exact state/field rules with an ambiguity corpus; validate interoperability independently of named heuristic tests.

gaps.title: Historical SynHX source identity and applicability
gaps.question: Which release/client/server configurations do the selected RCS trunk snapshots represent, and how do the default vendor branch and build options differ?
gaps.implementation_impact: A useful historical comparison could otherwise be generalized to all SynHX profiles or mixed build variants.
gaps.closure_criteria: Record archive lineage, selected/default revision relationship, relevant build flags and the exact peers to which each source observation applies.

gaps.title: Native conformance fixtures beyond one illustrative frame

sources.heading: Open compatibility gaps and QA requirements

gaps.question: Where are executable positive/negative fixtures for core handshake, authenticated login, both completion paths, errors and repeated-field handling?
gaps.implementation_impact: Static paths and a hand-counted example do not establish end-to-end interoperability or a regression oracle.
gaps.closure_criteria: Retain identified-peer/core-session captures and expected decoded/events results, with a reproducible fixture runner and packet provenance.

gaps.title: mxd implementation and test evidence

sources.heading: Reported mxd test coverage requiring verification
Open compatibility gaps and QA requirements

gaps.question: Do the named test/source references exist and pass at a recorded mxd revision, and do their assertions match the corrected protocol?
gaps.implementation_impact: The matrix cannot claim supported implementation from unexecuted citations that may encode old assumptions.
gaps.closure_criteria: Record checkout/revision, reviewed assertions, commands and outputs; fix or retire stale expectations and map passing cases to protocol requirements.

gaps.title: Release/proof acceptance criteria

sources.heading: Open compatibility gaps and QA requirements

gaps.question: What protocol subset, remaining-gap policy, client coverage and proof/test evidence are required for QA sign-off, and are the cited roadmap/proof items current?
gaps.implementation_impact: Neither an old roadmap pointer nor a correction disposition defines a release acceptance threshold.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish current sign-off criteria and owners at an identified revision, including deferred gaps and the scope/results of any Kani claims.

gaps.title: Portable, versioned evidence and document references
gaps.question: How will readers obtain the sibling mothra evidence, identify the corrected uncommitted document revision and follow stable claim/line references after edits?
gaps.implementation_impact: Working sibling-relative links and an old Git HEAD are not sufficient to reproduce a published baseline in another checkout.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish or package the hashed evidence and corrected docs with stable revision/artifact references; retain historical snapshots and define gap refresh/closure rules.
